title: Quantum metrology with undetected mid-infrared photons for applied non-destructive testing
authors: Paul Gattinger, Andreas W. Schell, Maja Buchegger, Markus Brandstetter, Ivan Zorin
abstract: Metrology with undetected photons is an emerging technique that leverages quantum effects and photon correlations (entanglement) to retrieve valuable information in a target spectral range (e.g., mid-infrared, mid-IR) using measurements in an easily accessible domain (e.g., visible, near-IR). The underlying quantum process of spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) is utilized to generate non-degenerate correlated signal and idler photons to serve as detection and probing photons, respectively. Sensing with undetected photons enables important advantages, such as ultra-low probe powers, room-temperature operation, and shot-noise-limited detection. In this contribution, we apply a quantum nonlinear interferometer based on an SPDC source to perform applied mid-IR spectroscopy, mid-IR microscopy, and mid-IR optical coherence tomography (OCT) as among the most promising techniques for quantum-based routine non-destructive testing. Moreover, we characterize the system, benchmark it against classical systems, and provide a prospective outlook for this new technology.
summary: The paper presents a novel quantum metrology technique for non-destructive testing that reads out mid-infrared sample information using visible/near-IR photons via correlated photon pairs generated by SPDC. By operating at ultra-low powers and achieving shot-noise-limited performance, this method offers a potential paradigm shift compared to expensive classical mid-IR instrumentation.
main_problem: The goal is to develop quantum metrology techniques for non-destructive testing (NDT) by reading out information about mid-infrared (mid-IR) samples using visible/near-IR photons.
main_result: The technique demonstrates ultra-low power impingement ($	ext{60 pW}$) and achieves shot-noise-limited performance, potentially surpassing classical methods for applications like QFTIR spectroscopy and OCT.
method: It utilizes a nonlinear interferometer based on spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) to generate correlated signal (detection) and idler (probing) photon pairs.
model_or_system: The experimental platform is a nonlinear Michelson-type interferometer pumped by a visible laser through a nonlinear crystal (e.g., ppKTP). The quantum correlation allows the mid-IR interaction to modulate the near-IR interference pattern.
key_observables: Signal photon interference visibility, Power Spectral Densities (PSDs), and B-scans from OCT imaging.
important_parameters: Ultra-low probe powers ($	ext{60 pW}$), shot-noise limit performance, and the energy conservation relation $\omega_p = \omega_s + \omega_i$.
main_assumptions: The technique assumes that quantum correlations can effectively transfer mid-IR sample information to the detectable visible/near-IR signal photons.
figures_summary: Figures show simulated PSDs, time-domain and Fourier-domain interferograms comparing open vs. blocked idler arms, and an experimental setup diagram using a HeNe laser reference.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the concept of undetected photon metrology, details the nonlinear interferometer setup for QFTIR/OCT, presents benchmarking against classical systems (showing superior SNR scaling), and concludes with future outlooks on increasing source brightness.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems as it demonstrates a practical application of quantum correlations (entanglement) in sensing, moving beyond fundamental demonstrations into routine NDT tools.

The inset depicts SPDC generation in a quasi-phase-matched configuration, where a pump beam propagating through a nonlinear crystal generates signal and idler beams.

Figure 2: Signal photon interferograms corresponding to the measurement modalities. a) high-pass filtered time-domain interferogram of the QFTIR modality (1 s scan time); b) Fourier-domain spectral interferogram (red line) for OCT with undetected photons (100 ms integration time); and sig- nal SPDC profile with idler photons blocked after first SPDC process (gray line).

Figure 3: Experimental multimodal system for metrology with undetected photons: nonlinear Michelson-type interferometer; 660 nm CW laser pumps a ppKTP crystal (Λ = 20.45 µm, L = 2.55 mm), launched via an alignment mirror (AM) and a cold mirror (CM), focused by an achromatic (AC) lens (f = 75 mm). The targeted idler spectral band (used for probing) spans 3000 cm-1 – 2360 cm-1 (3333 nm – 4237 nm), which corresponds to the signal range from approximately 780 nm to 820 nm (used for detection). The generated signal and idler beams are collimated via an off-axis parabolic mirror (OAPM, f = 75 mm) and separated by a dichroic mirror (DM).
